summary.text: A 62-year-old man with a history of surgically resected rectal mucinous adenocarcinoma (pT3N1M0) and ascending colon adenocarcinoma NOS (pT1bN0M0) at the age of 51 years presented with abdominal pain and vomiting. CT showed a mass lesion at the proximal jejunum, diagnosed as adenocarcinoma by biopsy. His family history was significant for Lynch syndrome: his sister had confirmed LS with colorectal and uterine corpus cancers, his mother and father had cancers, and his brother died of a brain tumor.

He underwent partial jejunectomy with lymph node dissection. The specimen showed adenocarcinoma NOS with a focal mucinous component, an intraepithelial lesion, venous and lymphatic invasion, a positive radial margin, negative proximal and distal margins, moderate tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes and stage IIIB disease (at least pT3, pN2 (4/5), cM0). Immunohistochemistry showed complete loss of MLH1, MSH2, MSH6 and PMS2, a null phenotype, whereas his previous colorectal cancers lacked only MSH2 and MSH6.

FoundationOne CDx profiling of the jejunal cancer found MSH2 F836fs*5, MSH2 D716fs*4 and MLH1 R659*, MSI-high status, a tumor mutation burden of 43 mutation/megabase and no BRAF V600E mutation, plus many other variants. A peripheral blood test confirmed MSH2 F836fs*5 as a germline variant also found in his sister, establishing Lynch syndrome; the parents were not tested.

He received postoperative immunotherapy with pembrolizumab. Seven months after surgery he required an operation for intestinal obstruction. Although the tumor was under control, he died 23 months after surgery, presumably from unrelated causes.

article_limitations: Table 1 rows other than Our case describe previously published cases cited by reference number; they are literature data, not roster patients, and are not recorded as patient facts.
Figure 1 pixels are recorded in the visual submission only; the caption states that all four MMR stains are deficient.
Genomic variants other than the MMR table cells are recorded in oncology.biomarkers only (no duplicate observation per variant); VAFs are recorded only where printed.
Stage context, disease extent and tumor disease status are not labelled in the source for any tumor and are left unknown.
Dose, schedule, route and duration of pembrolizumab are not stated; the operation for intestinal obstruction is not described beyond its indication and timing.
Discussion statements about published cases and author hypotheses (methylation, ARID1A/PIK3CA triggering, PMS2/MSH6-only testing) are not recorded as patient facts.
No supplementary material is listed for this article.
